one_line: A Tamil urban householder from the Keezhadi settlement on the Vaigai, c. 3rd century BCE–3rd century CE.

appearance.age_look: early 30s, medium height, sturdy but graceful build suggestive of active household work
appearance.face: soft oval face, warm brown complexion, straight nose, full lips, slightly arched brows, a small beauty mark near the left cheek, default expression calm and attentive with a hint of curiosity
appearance.hair: thick black hair oiled and parted at the center, drawn back into a low, neat bun at the nape; a simple narrow gold-toned hairpin securing the bun and a thin off‑white cotton headband tied around the crown
appearance.costume: a long ankle‑length unstitched cotton sari in muted brick‑red with a broad mustard‑yellow border, wrapped in an early Tamil style: pleats in front, lower end tucked at the waist, upper end drawn over the left shoulder and draped across the chest; beneath, a fitted short‑sleeved blouse in dull indigo cotton fully covering the torso; several plain bronze bangles on each wrist, a simple thin gold‑toned chain at the neck, small round stud earrings, and a modest waist cord of off‑white cotton; bare feet but clean, with a practical toe ring on each foot, overall textiles slightly worn but well‑kept and era‑appropriate to a prosperous yet ordinary urban family.
appearance.signature: a shallow reddish‑brown pottery tray held in both hands, containing a few everyday items: an iron sickle, a small cuboid terracotta gaming die, and a fragment of reddish pottery with a faint Tamil Brahmi graffiti mark, all carefully arranged to suggest the household’s work and literacy.

ref_desc: Keezhadi Urban Mother has a warm brown oval face with a cheek mole, black hair in a low bun with gold pin and headband, a brick‑red sari with mustard border over an indigo blouse, bronze jewellery, and carries a pottery tray holding an iron sickle, terracotta die, and graffiti sherd, in brick‑red, mustard, indigo, warm brown, and bronze tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style character model of the Keezhadi Urban Mother: an early‑30s Tamil woman with a warm brown oval face, small mole on her left cheek, straight nose, and calm, curious expression; her thick black hair is oiled, center‑parted, and pulled into a low bun at the nape, secured with a simple gold‑toned hairpin and a thin off‑white cotton headband around her crown. She wears an ankle‑length unstitched cotton brick‑red sari with a broad mustard‑yellow border, wrapped in an early Tamil style with front pleats, the lower end tucked at the waist and the upper end draped over her left shoulder and across her chest; under it, a modest short‑sleeved indigo cotton blouse fully covers her torso. On her wrists are several plain bronze bangles, at her neck a thin gold‑toned chain, on her ears small round stud earrings, and at her waist a simple off‑white cord; her bare feet show practical toe rings. In her hands she holds her signature prop: a shallow reddish‑brown pottery tray carrying a slightly curved iron sickle, a small cuboid terracotta gaming die, and a fragment of reddish pottery with a faint Tamil Brahmi graffiti mark. Show her in a neutral, front‑facing pose, plus side and back views, clearly presenting her face, hair arrangement, sari drape, blouse, jewellery, waist cord, toe rings, and the pottery tray with its contents, using a palette dominated by brick‑red, mustard yellow, warm brown, indigo blue, and bronze/gold.
